clue.text: Women consumed with superhero on run, admitting love bug

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the superhero comes after the run

parts.note: consumed in the sense of eaten gives ate
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the superhero takes the next piece inside

parts.note: Batman is the caped comic-book superhero
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tale of women eating with a superhero on the run who then confesses a fondness for an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts O inside BATMAN to make BOATMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The water boatman is an aquatic insect that rows itself along with oar-like legs, so it is a true bug.

clue.text: Needing time for support, because sibling beat mate

indicators.note: needing tells us the piece named next is wanted to finish the build, so it goes on the end

parts.note: as can mean because, as in 'as it was raining'
sis is short for sister, a sibling
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Someone needs time off for support because a brother or sister has attacked their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for support' reads as a hint at the role the answer fills, a helper giving support; the letters come from because, sibling, beat and time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a helper or junior worker, as in a plumber's mate, which is exactly an assistant.

clue.text: Inconclusive test cases of shell-like foreign objects

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the cut-short test wraps round the next piece
inconclusive means without a conclusion, so the word for test loses its last letter

parts.note: an exam is a test
shell-like is British slang for the ear, and otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A lab report on unresolved tests of strange shell-shaped items from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconclusive' leaves EXA, which 'cases' wraps round the ear word. 'Shell-like' is British slang for an ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are things from far away that are striking or unusual, a fair match for strange foreign objects.

clue.text: King in possession of large vessel

indicators.note: the king is held in the possession of the word for large, so it sits inside it

parts.note: big means large
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch who owns a large ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted sailing ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Oddball born in important Buddhist uprising becomes deviant

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the turned-round monk
in a down clue an uprising reads from bottom to top, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a lama is a senior Tibetan Buddhist monk or teacher

indicators.note: oddball signals that the letters of born are made odd, that is jumbled

explanation.surface: An eccentric child born during a revolt among senior Buddhists grows up to be a deviant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' gives AMAL and 'Oddball' gives BNOR, which goes 'in' after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant and abnormal both describe something departing from the usual standard.

clue.text: Bit quiet around ring policemen set up

indicators.note: around tells us the word for quiet surrounds the rest

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the plain-clothes branch of British police

explanation.surface: A little hush around a ring of police officers who have been framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' gives DIC, and 'around' wraps the word for quiet round O plus that.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount, and a bit means a small quantity too.

clue.text: Popular judge in North America is mercenary

indicators.note: in puts popular and judge inside the abbreviation for North America

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A well-liked American judge turns out to be in it for the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents in feudal Japan, often hired for espionage and assassination, so a mercenary.

clue.text: Artist's ear, item gent hacked with tip of razor

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
hacked means cut about roughly, so these letters are chopped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist's ear is a gentleman's item, cut off with a razor, recalling Van Gogh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' gives ENEMAGRITTE, and the letter from 'tip of razor' goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rene Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Almost outside choky protected by prison guard

indicators.note: protected by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: choky suggests something choked and mangled, so the remaining letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone nearly beyond the prison cell, kept safe by a jail warder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' leaves OUTSID; 'choky' rearranges that to USTODI, and 'protected by' sets it in the prison word. Choky is also British slang for prison, a deliberate distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper or protector, which is what a guard is.

clue.text: Ill will about launch, one glared heartlessly on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the ship comes last

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to hurl is to launch or throw
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the middle taken out

parts.note: shone means blazed with light, close to glared
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Bad feeling over a ship's launch where someone stared angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the O from SHONE, leaving SHNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Churlishness is rude, surly behaviour, close to the resentful attitude of ill will.

clue.text: Poet finished penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, like a pen around animals

parts.note: done means finished

explanation.surface: A poet who has completed writing a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, fitting a poet, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was the great English metaphysical poet of the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: International group's relief work is not declared

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an international group, and the 's adds an S
aid is help given in an emergency

explanation.surface: The United Nations' humanitarian programme goes unannounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unsaid has not been spoken or stated aloud, so not declared.

clue.text: Note king trapped in enclosure after wife remains

indicators.note: after places the rest following the wife's letter

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside the next piece

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A musical king locked in a cage after his wife has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is what is left of something destroyed, its broken remains.

clue.text: Content to sell a master's animals

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Happy to sell an expert's livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy, but it signals the letters held within 'sell a master's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American pack animals related to camels.

clue.text: Settled to reject obsession for overseas state

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: sat means settled, as a bird settles on a branch
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: Someone has settled down to shake off a fixation on a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia, overseas from the UK.

clue.text: A bishop among people giving recital

indicators.note: among means placed within the next piece

parts.note: a nation is a people
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop in the crowd at a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a telling or recounting of events, as is a recital.

clue.text: Oddly so, team on search to turn up loyal supporter

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters across the two words
in a down clue turn up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to trawl is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A strange team searching to find a dependable fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, reliable supporter of a cause or team.

clue.text: Really wet day clergyman initially disregarded

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the next word

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A rainy day when the vicar was overlooked at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially disregarded' drops C from CURATE. The definition reads as a verb: to really wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak thoroughly, to make really wet.

clue.text: Further copy is acquired by saving, after chapter's gone missing

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in by the next piece
gone missing means removed from the word

parts.note: rescue means saving

explanation.surface: An extra copy obtained through economies once a chapter vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone missing' leaves RESUE, and 'acquired by' sets the clue's own 'is' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a new release of a book or record, a further copy.

clue.text: Cleaner's fine contraption for drying

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencils
an airer is a clothes-drying frame

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady's lovely clothes horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is the comparative adjective. An airer is a frame for drying washing, common in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean clean or unblemished, as in a fair copy, so fairer is cleaner.

clue.text: Oral gel works rather fast

indicators.note: works means is worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mouth gel that acts quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo, fairly fast.

clue.text: Make arrangement for suit and plan for wedding

indicators.note: making an arrangement of letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Fitting out a suit and drawing up plans for the big day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a marriage ceremony, so a wedding.

clue.text: Projection for new leader of Greens

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An outlook on a new head of the Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a projecting spike, as on a fork, so a projection.

clue.text: One trapped by spy is yielding

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: a plant is an undercover agent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone caught by a secret agent gives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means flexible or easily bent, so yielding.

clue.text: Water pipe's hollow sound

definitions.meaning: a pipe for smoking in which the smoke passes through water
a deep ringing noise, like a bell

explanation.surface: The resonant noise a hookah makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is both a water pipe for smoking and the low resonant tone of a struck bell.

clue.text: Semi-liquid food left for hospital in stores

indicators.note: one thing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: shops are stores
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Sloppy food, swapped for hospital food in the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: In SHOPS the H is replaced by L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slops are watery or mushy food, often scraps fed to pigs.

clue.text: Next to confidant full of desires

indicators.note: full of means containing the next piece

parts.note: an aide is a trusted assistant
longs means yearns or desires

explanation.surface: Next to a trusted friend brimming with wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' splits the assistant word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside, so next to.

clue.text: Takes flight, like steward does for work

definitions.meaning: flees and hides away, like a fox bolting into its earth
a ground steward works on the ground at an airport rather than in the air

explanation.surface: An airline steward boarding a plane for a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes flight' and 'steward' both point to aircraft, but the first means fleeing, and the second is a ground steward who stays on the tarmac.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to ground is to hide from pursuers, which is a form of fleeing or taking flight.
